data.reasoning: The PKGBUILD is a standard Python package build from PyPI with a pinned SHA256 checksum for the source tarball. It uses standard build tools (python -m build, python -m installer) with no network operations, dynamic code evaluation, or obfuscated commands. The LICENSE file has SKIP checksum which is normal for locally-maintained files. No .install hooks or patches exist. The package installs only into $pkgdir as expected.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in the qwen model (HTTP 400 BadRequestError when processing .SRCINFO), not by genuine security concerns. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all three files and correctly identified them as safe. Both models agreed on the PKGBUILD and LICENSE assessments.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to process .SRCINFO due to LLM API error (HTTP 400), resulting in inconclusive verdict
learnings: Tool errors (API failures) should be handled gracefully - when one model encounters a transient error and another successfully completes the same audit, the successful audit should be weighted appropriately rather than treating the error as a genuine disagreement
For simple packages with only standard files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, LICENSE), a single successful model review is sufficient when it identifies no issues and follows standard packaging patterns
